title: Dorsett Residence Sri Hartamas: coming home through a hotel lobby.
videoTitle: PROPERTY REVIEW #476 | DORSETT RESIDENCE, SRI HARTAMAS
excerpt: An older tower that is part hotel, part residence, attached to Plaza Damas between Mont Kiara and Dutamas. Sean finds a roomy 657 sq ft unit, a still-polished lobby and common areas showing their age.
takeaways: Residents arrive through a hotel lobby and share the rooftop with hotel guests.
A 657 sq ft one-bedroom lists at about RM600,000, about RM900 psf, and rents for over RM3,000 furnished.
Heavy traffic, ageing common areas and dozens of competing towers nearby.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: One tower is split between a hotel and residences, each served by its own set of lifts, and both share the rooftop pool and gym. Residents come home through the hotel's lobby, which still looks impeccable. On the residential floors, three passenger lifts and a service lift serve 34 units, and the corridors were built to be air-conditioned, like a serviced residence.

Sean viewed a 657 sq ft one-bedroom unit, 4.3 m wide, with a 3.9 m kitchen run, a bedroom 6.3 by 4.2 m and a bathroom with two basins and a bathtub. Because the owner left the bedroom open, daylight reaches the living area, unlike the enclosed layout Sean saw at Dorsett Waterfront Subang.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: It is part of Plaza Damas 3 in Sri Hartamas, next to Mont Kiara and on the road to Dutamas and Publika, close to the courts and a street from Jalan Kuching. A bridge links it to a mall with a grocer, bookstore, gym, cafes and clinics, so residents can walk to almost everything. At 27 storeys it is the tallest building around, with views to the KL skyline and Damansara Heights. There is no rail link yet.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: This unit lists at about RM600,000, about RM900 psf, which Sean compares with new projects in Subang Jaya at RM900 to RM1,000 psf. Asking rent is over RM3,000 a month fully furnished; a couple working nearby could split it at about RM1,700 each. Owners he knows report steady demand from tenants staying three to six months, giving more than one way to let the unit.

standout.title: One tower, two uses
standout.body: The hotel and the residences share a single tower but have separate lift cores, so residents get a hotel arrival, with staff at the door and a check-in counter, without hotel guests on their floors. Both sides meet only at the shared rooftop.

pros: The location: the best of Mont Kiara and Dutamas, close to the city yet a street away from PJ, with highways such as DUKE, SPRINT and the Kerinchi Link all converging here.

A hotel and residence attached to Plaza Damas: residents still get the hotel arrival, and a bridge to the mall puts food, groceries, gyms, clinics and schools within walking distance. At 27 storeys it stands alone, without towers packed around it.

The architecture: one tower split by use with separate lift cores, corridors originally designed to be air-conditioned, and finishes that hold up well for their era. The unit is generous, brighter than the Subang version, and has a luxury-spec bathroom, and current rents still justify the price.
cons: Traffic: the crossroads into the area jam outside a short midday window, the roadside parking is always full, and there is no public transport yet, though future MRT stations may come. Many residents are lawyers and others who work nearby.
Age: the surrounding Plaza Damas buildings are old, and while the hotel lobby and the owner's unit look good, the residential corridors, lift lobbies, car park and facilities show their years.

Competition: 30 to 40 blocks in Mont Kiara, Society in Desa Sri Hartamas and new projects such as The Emersion give tenants plenty of choice. Even so, the location stays relevant thanks to the courts, Publika and the MRT to come, and rents remain high.

closing: A luxurious studio by today's standards, for tenants who work nearby and want to live without driving, as long as you accept an older building.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this October 2026 episode and its video description. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. An owner let Sean view the unit; the price and asking rent are from a listings site as he quoted them.
